candidates.name: Liechtenstein Museum
candidates.price: €25 (Stadtpalais), €20 (Gartenpalais); €38 (single ticket for both palaces); no discounts
candidates.content: A private collection of the Prince of Liechtenstein is exhibited in his former Viennese residences, which include the Stadtpalais (City Palace) and Gartenpalais (Garden Palace). The richly decorated picture gallery mainly exhibits

candidates.name: Pathologisch-anatomisches Bundesmuseum
candidates.content: Housed in a squat tower, which once was an insane asylum, the Narrenturm (Fool's Tower), this museum contains some of the dustier corners of the annals of medicine. You will find preserved hydrocephalic infants, wax castings of te

candidates.name: Josephinum
candidates.content: Founded by Emperor Joseph II as the Academy of Medico-Surgery, the building was completed in 1785 and houses nearly 1200 anatomical wax models commissioned by the emperor, along with medical documents and instruments. The Josephin

candidates.name: Freud Museum
candidates.content: This small museum is in Freud's historic flat where he practiced psychoanalysis for almost his whole life. However, the collection is limited mostly to documents of various kinds relating to Freud's life. Almost all of the flat's

candidates.name: Schönbrunn Palace
candidates.price: Grand Tour: €17.50 (adults), €11.50 (children); Imperial Tour: €14.20 (adults), €10.50 (children); entrance includes audio/written guide
candidates.content: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1996. It is the ultimate palace experience in Vienna, because the Habsburg summer palace can be found here. It is comparable in grandeur to Versailles and is definitely a must-see in

candidates.name: Hermesvilla
candidates.price: €7 (adults), €5 (seniors/students/Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19), free the first Su of every month
candidates.content: A late 19th-century palace in the Lainzer Tiergarten, a wooded area formerly used for hunting by the Habsburg family. The imperial apartments with their furnishings have been preserved, and feature murals by prominent Viennese art

candidates.name: Wiener Kriminalmuseum
candidates.price: Adult €8, student up to 16 with ID €4
candidates.content: This museum is dedicated to the history of police and the justice system, from the Middle Ages until World War II. Exhibits relating to famous Viennese criminals are included.

candidates.name: Stephansdom
candidates.hours: Daily Mon-Sat 06:00-22:00, Sun and holidays 07:00-22:00; visits for tourists: Mon-Sat 09:00-11:30, 13:00-16:30, Sun and holidays 13:00-16:300; tour of cathedral and treasury: Mon-Sat 10:30 (English), daily 15:00 (German)
candidates.content: Yet another patchwork of architectural styles, but predominantly Gothic. None of the original construction remains, the oldest extant sections are the thirteenth century Giant Gate (Riesentor) and Towers of the Heathens (Heidentür

candidates.name: Schatzkammer
candidates.alt: Imperial Treasury; aka the Secular and Ecclesiastical Treasures
candidates.price: €6 (as a combined ticket with the Museum of Fine Arts)
candidates.content: The best part of the Hofburg and an absolute must. It contains the Habsburgs' collection of jewels, crowns, and other valuables, perhaps the best on the Continent. Second only to a tour of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, of which th

candidates.name: Papyrusmuseum
candidates.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club and Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors), €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Globe and Esperanto Museums (listed below with the Austrian National Library)
candidates.content: One of the largest collections of its kind in the world, it includes nearly 180,000 manuscripts spanning 3,000 years of Egyptian history. 200 items are on permanent display.

candidates.name: Weltmuseum Wien
candidates.alt: formerly the Ethnological Museum / Museum für Völkerkunde
candidates.content: This collection encompasses many thousands of artifacts from around the globe. The most famous piece in its collection however is a headdress believed to have belonged to the last Aztec emperor Moctezuma.

candidates.name: Globenmuseum
candidates.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors), €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Esperanto and Papyrus Museums
candidates.content: The only museum of its type in the world, this museum contains a collection of 650 globes of all types, as well as a collection of nearly 300,000 historic maps.

candidates.name: Esperantomuseum
candidates.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors); €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Globe and Papyrus Museums
candidates.content: Founded in 1927, this museum houses a library and museum with displays illustrating the development and grammar of the modern invented language Esperanto.

candidates.name: Albertina
candidates.content: Once a palace, it is now the most popular exhibition space in Vienna, mainly for traditional modern art. The building itself is an experience as well. It is home to a valuable drawing collection, including many works of the German

candidates.name: Hofburgkapelle
candidates.price: Performances: seats €36/26/16, seats with no view €10; standing room only free (sold on Su at 08:30 before mass)
candidates.hours: Visiting hours: Mon Tue 10:00-14:00, Fri 11:00-13:00, closed holidays; Sun Mass: 09:15, seating no later than 09:00
candidates.content: The original chapel of the Palace, built in Gothic style 1447-1449, was made over in Baroque style. On Sundays and Catholic holidays (of which the Austrians celebrate many), the Court Musicians perform here. This group is made up

candidates.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
candidates.price: €14 (adults), €11 (concessions); admission includes entry to the Ephesos Museum, Collection of Historic Musical Instruments, and Collection of Arms and Armour (see listing below under New Palace)
candidates.content: One of the world's greatest art museums and in a palace that is a work of art itself. Serious art fans may wish to devote more than a day to its treasures. There is no other word to describe the Kunst other than mind-boggling. It

candidates.name: Naturhistorisches Museum
candidates.price: €10 (adults), €8 (seniors and Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €5 (students/apprentices/military), free (disabled and children under 19)
candidates.content: This museum was erected as a mirror to its twin museum, the Museum of Fine Arts. It exhibits various minerals, meteorites, fossils, stuffed animals, and skeleton reconstructions of dinosaurs and other. It also includes an anthropo

candidates.name: Winterpalais des Prinzen Eugen
candidates.content: This Baroque palace was built as a residence for Prince Eugene of Savoy, and later used for the Court Treasury and Ministry of Finance. It now houses period furnishings and exhibits detailing the biography of the prince and the hi

candidates.name: MAK
candidates.alt: Museum für angewandte Kunst / Austrian Museum of Applied Arts
candidates.price: €12 (adults), €10 (concessions), free (children and youth under 19); 50% discount on Tu from 18:00-22:00
candidates.content: The museum has the MAK Design Shop and a study collection. The museum emphasises design and decorative arts, and has a huge furniture collection. Early 20th century, especially Vienna Secession, and modern design are very well rep

candidates.name: Haus der Musik
candidates.content: This is a relatively new and special museum devoted to an interactive learning experience. It covers the history of the Vienne Philharmonic Orchestra, the history of Vienna as a centre of music making (Mozart, Haydn, Beethoven, Ma

candidates.name: Gemäldegalerie der Akademie der bildenden Künste
candidates.alt: Gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts
candidates.content: A gallery owned by the Academy of Fine Arts, to which Hitler applied to before he decided to change to politics. It offers some paintings by Rubens and Bosch. Most interesting are the Renaissance and medieval exponents.

candidates.name: Museum Postsparkasse
candidates.content: SIGNA, the owner of the Post Office Savings Bank building, runs the WAGNER:WERK Museum Postsparkasse. Opened by BAWAG P.S.K. in 2005, it's in the small banking hall. The museum and the main banking hall are open to visitors. At th

candidates.name: Bank Austria Kunstforum
candidates.content: This venue hosts special exhibits of internationally-renowned artists; past exhibits have displayed work by Egon Schiele, Oskar Kokoschka, Cézanne, Picasso, and Van Gogh.

candidates.name: Phantastenmuseum
candidates.content: An unusual museum dedicated to the work of the Vienna School of Fantastic Realism (Wiener Schule des Phantastischen Realismus), highlighting works by artists Ernst Fuchs, Arik Brauer, Rudolf Hausner, Wolfgang Hutter and Fritz Jans

candidates.name: Beethoven Pasqualatihaus
candidates.price: €4 (children and youth under 19), €3 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
candidates.content: This 18th-century building is atop the Mölker Bastei, one of the only remaining sections of the old city wall. For 8 years Beethoven lived in a 4th-floor apartment in this building, where he composed his 4th-8th symphonies as well

candidates.name: Jüdisches Museum Wien
candidates.price: €10 (adults), €8 (concessions), €5 (students), free (children under 15); includes admission to the branch on Judenplatz
candidates.hours: Sun-Fri 10:00-18:00; closed on Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur
candidates.content: A museum documenting the history of Vienna's substantial Jewish community which included Zweig, Freud, Herzl, Mahler, and Schoenberg. Three sites are available for one combined ticket: two museum sites and the main synagogue. Atta

candidates.name: Römermuseum
candidates.price: €6 (adults), €4 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
candidates.content: This museum houses a collection of artifacts from the Roman settlement of Vindobona, as Vienna was then known. There are Roman ruins in the cellar of the museum, first discovered during construction work in 1948, and for many year

candidates.name: Wiener Rathaus
candidates.price: Free; audioguides in English/French/Italian/Spanish available with ID
candidates.hours: Tours (in German) Mon Wed Fri 13:00, no registration required
candidates.content: Designed by Friedrich von Schmidt (the architect of the Cologne Cathedral) and completed in 1883, this is the most significant neo-Gothic building in Vienna, with a 103m-high clock tower. There is a very pleasant park with two fou

candidates.name: Burgtheater
candidates.hours: Guided tour Burgtheater – Behind the Scenes: Sep-Jun Mon-Thu 15:00 (German w/English summary), Fri-Sun 15:00 (German and English); guided tour Gustav Klimt – Main Staircases and Angelika Prokopp Foyer: Sep-Jun Fri-Sun 14:00 (German w/English summary)
candidates.content: The building was completed in 1888 and is home to one of the most respected German-language theaters, as well as the second-oldest theater in Europe. Non-German speaking visitors will find the building itself worth visiting, as th

candidates.name: Porgy & Bess
candidates.content: The Jazzclub features international Jazz artists. One can reserve seats in advance, which is recommended for special events. The bar offers good wine and some food too.

candidates.name: Wiener Eistraum
candidates.content: Every year from late January until the beginning of March a section of the park is transformed into an outdoor ice skating rink, with music. Ice skates can be rented directly onsite, and a baggage check is available. There are als

candidates.name: Donauinselfest
candidates.content: An open-air free music festival that takes place every June, and one of the largest of its kind in Europe. The festival is spread over an area of 6.5 km² with a number of music stages, hosting mostly Austrian and European pop musi

candidates.name: Strandbad Gänsehäufel
candidates.content: The Gänsehäufel is the biggest open air beach in Vienna, and is operated by the city. You can lie on the grass, swim in the Old Danube or swimming pools including a wave basin and a water slide. There are several other activities

candidates.name: Volksoper
candidates.content: The "People's Opera" is a venue for operettas, classical musicals, and ballet productions, as well as lighter traditional operas. Italian operas are often sung in German, and operas occasionally have English subtitles. Attendees u

candidates.name: WUK
candidates.content: WUK is a 12,000-m² space of culture, workshops, and social gathering. The cultural center regularly hosts concerts. The place was occupied by squatters in the early 1970s; these days it offers room for different cultural initiativ

candidates.name: Wiener Sängerknaben
candidates.hours: Not generally open to the public except on special occasions
candidates.content: Founded at the pleasure of the Habsburgs. On 20 July 1498, Emperor Maximilian decided to hire six singing boys, the first permanent boys choir attached to the court. He also made arrangements for their education – fringe benefits

candidates.name: MuTh
candidates.hours: Box office: Mon-Fri 16:00-18:00, and 1 hr before the start of a performance
candidates.content: A concert hall and multi-purpose auditorium for the Vienna Boys Choir, opened in 2012. A calendar of upcoming events is published here; tickets can be purchased at the door or online.

candidates.name: Messe Wien
candidates.content: Run by Reed Exhibitions, who operate fairgrounds throughout Austria, Vienna's fairgrounds are not as known for major events as the ones in Frankfurt, Munich or Hannover, but still play host to many events important to the Austrian

candidates.name: Ernst-Happel-Stadion
candidates.content: Austria's biggest stadium (capacity 50.000) is frequently hosting major sports events like soccer (Austrian National Squad; Rapid Wien; Euro League and Champions League), track-and-fields, as well as the occasional concert (e.g. B

candidates.name: Wiener Staatsoper
candidates.content: Probably the most-beloved symbol of Viennese arts, and one of the first buildings to be rebuilt in the postwar era. It was built from 1861-1869 under the direction of architects Eduard van der Nüll and August von Siccardsburg for

candidates.name: Wiener Philharmoniker
candidates.content: Considered one of the world's best orchestras, subscription tickets are notoriously difficult to get with a waiting list lasting up to 13 years. Individual tickets however are available in limited numbers online from the Musikvere

candidates.name: Musikverein
candidates.content: Home to the Vienna Philharmonic, and venue for a wide range of other classical music performances. Its largest hall, the Großer Musikvereinssaal (Goldener Saal) is considered to be one of the world's finest concert halls. For visi

candidates.name: Wiener Hofburg Orchester
candidates.hours: Three times a week May - mid Oct
candidates.content: Performs live. The program features the most famous waltz and operetta melodies by "the King of the Waltz", Johann Strauss, Franz Léhar and opera aries by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. It is led by conductor Gert Hofbauer, is composed

candidates.name: Zentralbad Wien
candidates.content: This historic men's sauna was opened in 1889 and since then has been considered to be the premiere bathing spots of Vienna. Visitors have included Habsburg royalty and modern day celebrities.

candidates.name: Theater in der Josefstadt
candidates.content: Opened in 1776, this is the oldest continually-operating theater in Vienna. At its reopening following a remodeling in 1822 Beethoven directed his commissioned piece Die Weihe des Hauses (The Consecration of the House). Since 1858

candidates.name: Arena
candidates.content: The arena is one of the biggest concert and alternative culture places. The slaughterhouse got squatted in 1976 and operates since as culture center. FM4 hosts here its annual birthday party. The programme lists the performing art

candidates.name: Theater an der Wien
candidates.content: This historic theater was founded by Emanuel Schikaneder (best known as Mozart's librettist for The Magic Flute). The building was designed by Franz Jäger, and completed in 1801. Since opening it has been the venue for many histor

candidates.name: Apollo Kino
candidates.content: A Cineplexx theater with plenty of choices including original versions. The cinema opened here in 1905. According to seat numbers it is one of the biggest in Vienna.

candidates.name: Schlumberger Kellerwelten
candidates.content: The tour in the cellar of one of the biggest Austrian "Sekt" producers takes approximately an hour, and there are up to 5 different glasses for tasting included.

candidates.name: Schweizerhaus
candidates.content: Large beer garden, some say they have the best beer in Vienna and they also offer traditional Austrian dishes at moderate prices. Also well-known for its excellent Stelze (knuckle of pork).

candidates.name: Loos American Bar
candidates.alt: Loos Bar, Kärntner Bar, American Bar
candidates.content: Built in 1908, this small bar was designed by Adolf Loos and inspired by his stay in the US from 1893-1896, and will delight fans of Art Deco. Famous for its architecture and interior decoration, it is a time warp of Vienna from 1

candidates.name: Bermuda Triangle
candidates.content: A night-life area popular for young people as the alcoholic beverages are cheap.

candidates.name: Wein & Co
candidates.content: A chain shop for wine lovers featuring a wine bar in every location. Shop locations include Naschmarkt, Mariahilfer Straße, near Burggarten and near Stephansplatz.

candidates.name: Café Bräunerhof
candidates.content: Thomas Bernhard used to come here daily as do many other Viennese literate. It exists since more than 35 years. Happily expect Viennese grumpy senior waiters.

candidates.name: Café Central
candidates.content: One of the most famous Vienna coffee houses, which opened in 1876, has been authentically restored. Beautiful premises inside the Palais Ferstel, it is too touristy and a bit more expensive for having a meal, but can be worth it f

candidates.name: Café Diglas
candidates.content: Famous traditional coffeehouse, and equally good place for having a meal. They opened a second branch on Fleischmarkt.

candidates.name: Café Hawelka
candidates.content: One of the most famous intellectual cafes in Vienna. Established in 1939. Surprisingly cheap for its location and its fame and can get quite cozy. Josephine Hawelka (former owner, deceased 2005) was proud of the marriages she caus

candidates.name: Café Landtmann
candidates.price: Breakfast sets €7-12.50, menu of the day around €11, starters €8-14, soup €4-8, schnitzel €20, coffee €4
candidates.hours: 07:30-24:00; all menus until 11:30, except Franz Landtmann served until 15:00
candidates.content: Old café, cozy and romantic. Used to be frequented by Sigmund Freud. Delicious food and desserts.

candidates.name: Café Museum
candidates.content: This cafe was designed by famous architect Adolf Loos, however the interior has been entirely refitted (most recently from 2010). Serves food, coffee, teas, and other drinks. Casual, quiet atmosphere.

candidates.name: Conditorei Sluka
candidates.content: A very traditional small Viennese café, opened at the end of the 19th century by Josef and Josefine Sluka, serves excellent pastries and bread. To the breakfast you can order oeuf poché. The choice on the menu is adjusted accordin

candidates.name: Demel
candidates.content: Café and confectionary shop. Good pastries are ubiquitous in Vienna, but Demel is considered by many to have the best of all and indeed was once the pastry caterer to the Imperial household. As a result of this it is usually jamme

candidates.name: Vollpension
candidates.content: Intergenerational café run as a social business: the cakes are baked by senior citizens to their own family recipes and served in a vintage living-room setting. Vegetarian lunch menu on weekdays, shaded outdoor seating in summer,

candidates.name: Lusthaus
candidates.hours: Oct-Apr: Thu-Tue 12:00-18:00; May-Sep: Mon Tue Thu Fri 12:00-23:00, Sat Sun holidays 12:00-18:00
candidates.content: Built in 1784 as a lodge for imperial hunting parties, the unusual octagonal building has served as a restaurant since the end of the monarchy. Serves traditional Austrian fare.

candidates.name: Zum roten Bären
candidates.content: The restaurant serves Austrian food classics combined with Slovenian food with great quality cooked by Hans Bodingbauer. It has Černá-Hora beer and interesting white wines per glass sold cheaply.

candidates.name: Pizza Mari
candidates.content: A very authentic and chic napolitanian pizza parlor. Large, delicious pizzas and a range of Italian food. The wine card has interesting Austrian white wine choices.

candidates.name: Inigo
candidates.price: Mains around €10, average dinner with a glass of wine €20 (June 2016)
candidates.content: Modern and diverse cuisine, not crowded but most visitors are local. Charming modern interior instead of imperial chic. Overall, a rare combination of features. Menu has equal parts for vegetarians and carnivores. Friendly to fami

candidates.name: Plachutta
candidates.content: A very nice restaurant that specialises in beef (claimed to be only local and from trusted farmers) and has some flavour of traditional Austrian cuisine. Try the Tafelspitz, it comes in a copper pan and still is in the soup it was

candidates.name: Schnitzelwirt Schmidt
candidates.content: The traditional Viennese food is excellent and served in truly prodigious portions. The Bauernschmaus (Farmer's Feast), a nearly incapacitatingly large schnitzel plate, which in combination with any of the wonderful on-tap beers,

candidates.name: Vorstadtwirt
candidates.content: Classic Viennese cuisine in a typical old-style neighbourhood pub with old and well preserved wooden walls. Small regular menu but vast, often changing, seasonal selection of dishes.

candidates.name: Der Ringsmuth
candidates.content: Der Ringsmuth serves traditional Austrian cuisine (including tasty Wiener Schnitzel of both pork and veal) among other dishes. Spacious, with pleasant minimalistic decor. Easily accessible as it's pretty much right next to the Wie

candidates.name: Kent Restaurant
candidates.content: At first approach, this looks like a greasy kebab joint strictly for Turks, but struggle past the first room and you will find a large garden and huge restaurant serving moderately priced food with an infinite supply of free Turki

candidates.name: The Highlander
candidates.content: Offers own beer and a nice variety of dishes, including vegetarian dishes, at a small square. Might not be one of the cheapest in the cheap section, but definitely worth the price.

candidates.name: Wiener Deewan
candidates.content: Young, urban Pakistani restaurant. All you can eat, pay as you wish. You can mix your own menu from a variety of curries, meat, rice, salads, and sauces. Vegetarians will have good choices.

candidates.name: Esterházykeller
candidates.content: Atmospheric old (since 1683) cellar restaurant serving good, cheap, wine, beer, and simple traditional food. Prices budget to moderate. A good place to go if you just want a drink and some grub, but still want to enjoy some local

candidates.name: Karmelitermarkt
candidates.hours: Market Mon-Fri 06:00-19:30, Sat 06:00-17:00; dining Mon-Sat 06:00-23:00. Closed Sun and public holidays
candidates.content: This traditional fruits and vegetable market is the heart of the trendy, hip Karmeliterviertel neighbourhood. There are still some classic shops (including a horsemeat-butcher), but most of the stalls now house trendy restaurants

candidates.name: Hannovermarkt
candidates.hours: Market Mon-Fri 06:00-19:30, Sat 06:00-17:00; dining Mon-Sat 06:00-23:00; closed Sun and public holidays
candidates.content: When looking for a real food market, check out the Hannovermarkt. It has many stalls for fruit, vegetables, meat and fish – mostly run by migrants – and the purist will not be bothered by hipster-cafés.

candidates.name: Landstraßer Haupstraße
candidates.content: A relatively upper middle-class neighbourhood shopping street, with a wide variety of business from pubs and clubs to organic shops to second-hand stores. The Rochus Market, Rochusmarkt, and a shopping arcade are located along thi

candidates.name: Naschmarkt
candidates.content: This is the largest of Vienna's 22 market places and provides a unique blend of typical Vienna costumely and oriental flair. Stroll through the market and be part of the amazing ambiance. If you like to cook, you will find all the

candidates.name: Favoritenstraße
candidates.content: The pedestrian zone with international clothing store chains as well as lots of cafes and restaurants in the area around Keplerplatz (U1) and becomes an immigrant shopping area after the busy Reumanplatz (U1) station. Adjacent to

december.text: The classic overnight train Metropol from Berlin was discontinued in December 2017, but returned as a ÖBB Nightjet train in December 2018, running via Prague and Dresden.
Turkey: No direct trains run from Vienna to Turkey, although if you're in for an adventure, there is a train from Villach and Istanbul.

There are 21 markets with stands and small characteristically Viennese hut-like shops that are open daily (except Sunday). thumb|Belvedere Christmas Market

Open from November 15 or 20 to December 23 or 24, most Viennese Christmas Markets ("Christkindlmarkt", "Adventmarkt" or simply "Weihnachtsmarkt") are not so much for shopping as for eating and drinking. From midday until the late hours of the night, people gather at Christmas markets to drink mulled wine, punch, and ch
Resselpark/Karlsplatz - A small, alternative and more rambunctious Christmas market in front of Karlskirche.
Further afield a famous and overly bustling Christmas market may be found at Grafenegg castle. Entry is €7, children under the age of 12 are free.
Roast chestnuts ("Maroni") are a common snack during the colder months, and are sold from street stalls all over the city, especially near train and U-Bahn stations, and at Christmas markets.

Glühwein is hot, sweetened red wine with cinnamon and cloves, served from stalls at Christmas markets. Belvedere: Another addition to the city's Christmas markets, the market in front of the Belvedere palace is spacious and emphasizes the homespun.

Hietzing is a very safe district of Vienna. Although the subway stop Hietzing may look a bit shady at night, the situation is never problematic, and walking around at night is very safe. The worst crime prevalent here is pickpocketing, which only happens in Schönbrunn. If you do go to Schönbrunn, especially during the

Ice skating: At the Wiener Eislaufverein in winter time one can skate on a big 6000 m² square.
